primary_reader_tasks: understand the event sequence and duration

observed_symptoms: generic visual hierarchy
content clustered toward the upper page
weak motif identity
iteration_history.learning: Content correctness does not establish visual identity or reader navigation.

observed_symptoms: palette and font hierarchy improved
metadata and list groups still looked templated
iteration_history.learning: Color changes alone do not solve layout composition.

observed_symptoms: stronger section labels
repeated boxed or card-like groups remained
iteration_history.learning: Repeated rectangles can create a rigid visual grammar even when the palette is coherent.

observed_symptoms: open editorial lists improved the page
manual pagination created a blank page
iteration_history.learning: Every layout change must be rendered again and checked for page-flow regressions.

observed_symptoms: pagination recovered
composition still appeared flat and mechanically repetitive
iteration_history.learning: A technical layout fix does not establish visual acceptance.

observed_symptoms: open three-page editorial structure
motif family repeated across cover, materials and timeline
metadata and narrative lists no longer enclosed as cards
schedule expressed as a curved sequence
iteration_history.learning: Motif continuity, varied rhythm and purposeful negative space can add character without inventing content.

observed_symptoms: T5's organic-motif composition was judged too decorative and too recognizable as a generic AI-style design treatment
oversized display typography, celestial illustration, repeated decorative marks, gold-green accents and a curved timeline formed a conspicuous visual signature
the decoration was not grounded in an actual organization identity, supplied logo or confirmed brand system
iteration_history.learning: A visually polished page can still look synthetic when decorative motifs are more prominent than the document's genre and purpose. Do not invent a brand or ornamental system to manufacture visual interest. Return to the conventions of the supplied document family and let information hierarchy carry the design.

observed_symptoms: conventional Times New Roman typography and plain bold section labels
centered formal title and simple subtitle without illustration
ordinary numbered lists and label-value metadata
one understated rule and one functional table for the schedule
decorative motifs, repeated cards, display lettering and ornamental section numbering removed
iteration_history.learning: Genre fidelity is a stronger default than decorative novelty for an organizational TOR. Improve spacing, alignment and reading rhythm within familiar office-document conventions; do not confuse visual restraint with cramped or unfinished layout.

open_design_risks: Reader-task usability has not been tested with representative readers.
The understated treatment is a candidate for this TOR, not a universal template for other document families.
Organization-specific marks or brand colors must only be used when supplied or verified.

reusable_controls: Separate content integrity, layout integrity, visual composition and reader usability gates.
Do not encode a universal attention-span duration.
Choose visual hierarchy around actual reader tasks.
Avoid repeated cards or rectangular frames when open typography, columns or timelines communicate the content more clearly.
Use a motif family with semantic or identity relevance; do not paste unrelated decoration onto a template.
Assess whitespace by function and page-to-page rhythm, not by a universal fill percentage.
Render and inspect every page after meaningful revisions.
Keep eye-tracking status NOT_MEASURED unless eye-tracking evidence exists.
limitations: This is one sanitized event-TOR iteration case and is not representative of every institution, discipline or document family.
The public learning record contains no original TOR text, identity values, source files, filenames or hashes.
Visual composition proxy results are not a measure of gaze, comprehension or aesthetic preference.
